name: Strömsund Bridge
facts: Strömsund Bridge, a 332‑meter cable‑stayed marvel, opened in 1956, becoming the world’s first large modern cable‑stayed bridge and earning the nickname “Jämtland’s Golden Gate.”
Designed in 1953 by German steel company Demag, the bridge’s 182‑meter main span showcases pioneering engineering that outpaced earlier concepts by the late‑dead engineer Franz Dischinger.

Built jointly by Demag and Swedish concrete firm Skanska, Strömsund Bridge carries the E45 highway across Ströms vattudal, linking rural communities in Jämtland with Sweden’s north‑south traffic artery.
